Subject: Clarify: Log retention/filtering & PII masking (Greenline Health)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can finalize the SOW and security appendix. I wanted to put these in one place for the internal and engineering folks to take action.

High-level summary (from our notes):
- Use case: customer support assistant in production that logs request/response metadata for debugging and analytics; Greenline will not persist full free-text prompts longer than necessary.
- Requirements called out on the call: PII suppression in both request & response logs, ability to drop or pseudonymize trace IDs in forwarded telemetry, and a 90-day max retention for structured logs with a 30-day hot window.

Clarifying questions / asks (can you confirm each):
1) Which specific fields in the request body must be redact-on-ingest vs. redacted for storage? Example: full patient name vs. client-assigned ID.
2) Residency: do logs need to be written only to the us-west region or is cross-region replication allowed for backup?
3) Trace IDs: do you need the raw trace_id to persist for troubleshooting, or is a one-way hashed value acceptable if we provide a reversible HSM-backed mapping for approved support audits?
4) Audit/evidence: you mentioned SOC2 artifacts — please confirm whether you want a separate, read-only audit log stream delivered to your S3 bucket.

What we can offer immediately (short answers):
- Redaction rules: prefix-only indexing, tokenization-plus-mask, and on-the-fly regex suppression at the edge proxy.
- Trace IDs: option A) keep raw trace_id in private Dedicated deployments; option B) store hashed trace_id (SHA-256) in hosted with per-account salt; option C) drop trace_id entirely and surface only transaction IDs created by you.
- Retention: configurable per-account retention (30/90/365 days) with roll-off and cold-archive options.

Next steps (proposed):
- Alex: confirm answers to Q1–Q4 by Wed EOD PST (11/17).
- Aditya: draft a short tech note on our log redact pipeline and sample JSON schemas by Thu (11/18).
- Marissa: prep a scoped SOW addendum for the retention/obfuscation controls.

Attachments: I attached a short proposal PDF and an XLSX with the placeholders you can fill in for fields that must be redacted.

Thanks —
Soojin

Thanks Soojin — helpful summary. Quick answers inline.

On Mon, Nov 14, 2027 at 8:02 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Which specific fields in the request body must be redact-on-ingest vs. redacted for storage?

For us: full patient name and SSN must be redacted on ingest. Phone and email should be tokenized (we still want search by hashed phone). Patient ID (our internal GUID) should be retained. I'll upload a sample exported schema (PII_fields.csv) to the Drive folder.

> 2) Residency: do logs need to be written only to the us-west region or is cross-region replication allowed for backup?

We prefer no cross-region replicas of logs containing PII. Backups can be cross-region only if PII fields are excluded.

> 3) Trace IDs: do you need the raw trace_id to persist for troubleshooting, or is a one-way hashed value acceptable if we provide a reversible HSM-backed mapping for approved support audits?

We'd accept a hashed trace_id for normal operations, but must be able to request a reversible mapping on a per-audit basis (legal/medical investigations). That mapping must be controlled via a documented approval process.

> 4) Audit/evidence: you mentioned SOC2 artifacts — please confirm whether you want a separate, read-only audit log stream delivered to your S3 bucket.

Yes — read-only audit stream to our S3 (us-west) is required. We'll share bucket and write-only credentials when we finalize the agreement.

Two small extra asks:
- Can Redwood suppress request headers that may contain third-party Google analytics cookies or partner trace headers before logs are persisted?
- We will need explicit documentation of what gets scrubbed vs. what gets redacted (regex, ruleset examples).

I'll get the PII_fields.csv in the Drive by EOD.

—Alex

Looping in a quick technical plan based on Alex's answers. High level:

1) Ingest pipeline changes (edge proxy):
- Apply ingestion ruleset JSON (per-account) that runs regex redaction for name/SSN at the proxy and replaces with "[REDACTED]".
- Tokenization service: phone/email hashed with HMAC-SHA256 using account-specific salt stored in KMS. Hash searchable but irreversible for normal ops.
- Header-suppression: we can configure a headers allowlist and drop any header not on the list before logs are emitted. This will remove third-party analytics cookies and partner trace headers.

2) Trace ID handling:
- Default behavior (hosted): store salted SHA-256 trace fingerprint. Support path to request HSM-backed reversible mapping (requires signed approval workflow; 7-day TTL for mapping keys).
- Dedicated/Private option: keep raw trace_id within the private cluster and provide secure tooling for re-identification.

3) Retention/replication:
- Implement per-account retention policy: 30/90/365 day buckets. PII fields redacted-on-ingest are not included in backups.
- Cross-region replication: disabled by default for buckets flagged with PII; manual exception process available.

4) Audit delivery:
- We can push a read-only audit stream to Greenline S3 with per-object encryption and lifecycle policy. Delivery will be incremental (hourly).

Open questions for the team:
- We should provide a sample ruleset and a small in-prod test (staging) where Alex's PII_fields.csv is ingested so Greenline can validate masking behavior.
- Need Marissa to confirm commercial implications for the reversible audit mapping (this may push customer to Dedicated contract).

I can draft the ruleset and a sample payload by Thu 11/18.

-Aditya
